Fiesta Bowl 2026: parking, the parade and getting there

A dependable Fiesta Bowl ride from Scottsdale Sprinters begins with the official event information, a realistic rider count, and one transportation lead. This guide uses published organizer or venue facts, leaves unannounced details unguessed, and turns the day into a written pickup, arrival, communication and return plan.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

When is the Fiesta Bowl?

The 2026-27 Vrbo Fiesta Bowl is the CFP quarterfinal on Wednesday, December 30, 2026, at 5:30 pm Arizona time at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, so planners can anchor the service date now and should recheck the official page before confirming pickup times. Use the official source linked below as the date authority. Artist schedules, participating teams, kickoff times, venue hours, and traffic instructions may arrive later than the date itself. Do not build a pickup plan around an unofficial calendar listing. The transportation lead should recheck the organizer page at booking, again as the date approaches, and on the service day. Fiesta Sports Foundation schedules this game as the CFP quarterfinal on Wednesday, December 30, 2026, at 5:30 pm Arizona time at State Farm Stadium. The College Football Playoff lists that same kickoff as 7:30 p.m. ET, because Arizona does not observe daylight saving time. Recheck both official pages if the organizer updates event information. Publishing early matters because a large-event route needs more than a car reservation. The group may still need admission passes, lodging, a meeting point, and agreement about who rides home. An article published ahead of the event gives planners time to compare vehicle sizes, collect guest commitments, and confirm current access rules without inventing details. When a date or time remains unannounced, the quote request can still describe the expected city, group size, hotel area, and service pattern. Mark uncertain times as planning placeholders, not confirmed instructions. The reservations team can update the service window once the official organizer publishes the missing information.

Which vehicle size fits a Fiesta Bowl group?

For the Fiesta Bowl, compare 9 published capacity bands from 6 through 56 passengers, then choose from the committed rider count and what the group will carry; the largest seat number is not automatically the best choice when people have permitted gear, accessibility needs, or hotel luggage. The fleet table uses current published information for each displayed name, maximum seated capacity, hourly rate, and minimum. A Executive Black Sprinter seats 14; a 56-Passenger Motorcoach seats 56. Larger groups can use multiple coordinated vehicles when one vehicle does not fit the rider count or what guests will carry. Count the riders for each direction. The outbound group may be larger than the return group, especially when some guests camp, stay near the venue, or leave with family. Give every return rider a specific vehicle or wave. “We will decide later” is not a useful manifest when a large event crowd is leaving at once. A Fiesta Bowl group usually needs one count for the stadium arrival and another for the return. Remove anyone using a separate postgame plan before assigning seats, and ask about mobility devices or personal items that affect fit. The vehicle choice should follow those confirmed movements, not the number of people included in a broader game-day gathering. Tell the reservations team about permitted personal items before choosing the vehicle. Event bag and chair rules belong to the organizer, and vehicle fit belongs to the operator. Something allowed into the venue may still consume meaningful cabin space. Keep aisles and exits clear, and never use an advertised seat count as a substitute for a real load review.

Plan 1 documented arrival route to State Farm Stadium, with the chauffeur following current event staff, traffic control, and the organizer's published instructions; a saved gate name from an earlier event is not reliable enough for dispatch, so this guide uses only access details supported by an official source. What should the Fiesta Bowl itinerary include?

Write 7 lines into the Fiesta Bowl itinerary: guest ready time, vehicle departure, venue arrival target, primary contact, official address, post-event meeting instructions, and final roll time, then keep optional meals or gatherings in a separate section so riders can immediately see the commitments that affect transportation. For game day, the outline is hotel pickup, an optional pregame stop only if scheduled, arrival ahead of the 5:30 p.m. Arizona kickoff, a security and admission buffer, a postgame pedestrian regrouping point, and the confirmed vehicle pickup. Turn that outline into clock times only after official hours or kickoff information is available. A useful schedule works backward from the desired arrival, adding expected loading and a conservative traffic allowance. Avoid publishing a universal drive time because origin, closures, day of week, and event operations all change it. Build the December 30 itinerary backward from the 5:30 p.m. Arizona kickoff at 1 Cardinals Drive in Glendale. If the group also wants the parade, schedule it as its own service: Saturday, January 2, 2027, at 10 a.m., starting at Central and Montebello in Phoenix, after the game. The 2027 parade route, grandstands, and street closures are announced closer to the date. The ready time is when guests are physically at the pickup point with everything they will take. It is not the time they begin leaving hotel rooms. The transportation lead should arrive earlier, check the manifest, and contact missing riders. Decide in advance who has authority to hold the vehicle and how long the schedule can absorb that hold. Include one contingency sentence: if the group becomes separated, each rider follows the written meeting instruction and contacts the transportation lead. Do not create multiple competing pins during the event. A simple, approved plan is easier to execute when cellular service is busy and the surrounding streets are controlled.

How should pickup after the Fiesta Bowl work?

Use 2 checkpoints after the Fiesta Bowl: the group first gathers at a pedestrian meeting place permitted by venue instructions, then the transportation lead confirms the vehicle’s active pickup point before anyone walks toward it, preventing riders from chasing a moving vehicle through controlled traffic or crowd flow. The chauffeur may be directed away from the arrival location or held until traffic staff release a lane. That is normal large-event operations, not a reason for guests to enter a roadway. The lead stays with the group, keeps a headcount, and waits for a confirmed message about where and when to move. Set expectations before arrival: the vehicle cannot stop wherever a phone pin lands, and an event's official traffic team controls access. Guests should wear appropriate footwear for the walk they can reasonably expect around a large venue and keep enough phone charge for post-event messages. Anyone leaving separately tells the transportation lead. Postgame traffic at State Farm Stadium can be directed differently from arrival, so the lead should not send the group toward the Black Lot until the active pickup instruction is confirmed. Assemble first in a safe pedestrian place permitted by venue guidance, complete the headcount, and move only after the vehicle location and route are understood. For multiple return waves, label vehicles and destinations clearly. A hotel shuttle and a local-home shuttle should not rely on guests recognizing a driver in a crowd. Use the vehicle name, lead name, and destination list. The final sweep verifies the manifest before departure rather than waiting on people who changed plans without notice.

How is Fiesta Bowl transportation priced per person?

For 12 Fiesta Bowl riders sharing the Executive Black Sprinter across 5 billed hours, the published $145-per-hour rate is about $60 per person before tax for the complete shared ride; actual pricing changes with the vehicle, duration, itinerary, and confirmed service plan. That example is arithmetic, not a flat event fare: hourly rate multiplied by billed hours, divided by riders. It gives a group a common basis for comparison while staying aligned with the published rate. If only ten people ride, divide across ten. If the group needs a larger vehicle or a longer service window, request the matching calculation. A complete plan may include a continuous vehicle, separated inbound and outbound transfers, or several hotel waves. Each structure uses time differently. Describe the actual service pattern when asking for a quote instead of requesting “round trip” and leaving a many-hour gap unexplained. The reservations team can then price the schedule that the group expects. A Fiesta Bowl quote should state whether the vehicle remains with the group, performs separate inbound and outbound transfers, or serves more than one hotel wave. Price examples based on five hours are comparisons only; the written quote must reflect the December 30 schedule, confirmed stadium access, rider count, and actual time requested. Per-person math is most useful after the rider list stabilizes. Name one person to collect shares and one person to manage the manifest; they can be the same person, but neither job should fall to the chauffeur. The transportation service moves the confirmed group while the lead owns internal guest decisions.

What are the most common Fiesta Bowl transportation questions?

Most Fiesta Bowl groups need 4 answers before booking: the official date status, the number of committed riders, the venue's current vehicle instructions, and the return meeting process; the FAQ below addresses those points without promising an unpublished time, access route, parking privilege, or gate.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Fiesta Bowl played?

At State Farm Stadium, 1 Cardinals Drive, Glendale, Arizona 85305. The 2026-27 game is the College Football Playoff quarterfinal.

What time does the Fiesta Bowl start?

5:30 p.m. Arizona time on Wednesday, December 30, 2026, the only College Football Playoff game that day. The College Football Playoff lists the same kickoff as 7:30 p.m. Eastern, because Arizona does not observe daylight saving time.

Where is the best place to park for the Fiesta Bowl?

The official 2026-27 parking map lists the West, North and East Preferred lots; the East Lot, Lot F and oversized parking; the West Lot, W2, the Great Lawn and the Yellow Lot; and the Black and Blue Lots, on game day only. Last season the lots opened at 11:30 a.m. and closed one hour after the game; this season’s times are announced closer to the date. With a chauffeured ride, nobody in the group parks.

Where do I buy Fiesta Bowl parking?

Parking passes are sold through the Fiesta Sports Foundation’s official parking link (SeatGeek), and State Farm Stadium’s lots take cards only.

How do I buy seats for the Fiesta Bowl?

From the Fiesta Sports Foundation, which runs the bowl: call 480.350.0911 or use its official website. A ride booking does not include game admission or a parking pass.

When is the Fiesta Bowl Parade?

Saturday, January 2, 2027, starting at 10 a.m. It is the 54th annual parade, admission is free, and it comes after the bowl games, not before.

Where does the Fiesta Bowl Parade go?

It is a 1.5-mile march through Central Phoenix, starting at North Central Avenue and Montebello Avenue, Phoenix 85012. The full 2027 route, grandstands and street closures are announced closer to the date.

Can we book a ride to the Fiesta Bowl Parade?

Yes, as its own ride on Saturday morning. Your chauffeur picks the group up at the hotel or home, drops everyone near the start at North Central Avenue and Montebello Avenue where police and event staff direct, and brings the group back when you are done.

Does a transportation booking include Fiesta Bowl admission?

No. Admission passes, wristbands, parking credentials, and venue entry are separate. Purchase and verify them only through the event’s official channels.

Can the vehicle wait next to the venue?

Only where current event operations permit it. Staging and pickup instructions can change, so the chauffeur follows venue staff and the transportation lead shares the confirmed meeting plan.

Can a group bring chairs, coolers, or bags?

Check the organizer’s current allowed-items policy first, then tell the reservations team exactly what the group will carry so vehicle fit can be reviewed.

What if the official event time changes?

Have the transportation lead contact the reservations team promptly. A revised service window is not assumed until the change is acknowledged and the updated plan is confirmed.
